answer: Tie voting weight and payouts to a public history signed by independent peers, so each identity must earn endorsements over many separate tasks before it counts fully. A lone operator can mint names quickly, but cannot forge a long, varied record; like a quill leaving distinct strokes, each endorsement is traceable. Fakes arriving as a sudden tide would stand out against the calm lagoon of gradual, verifiable trust and be throttled before they can steer outcomes.
